nodes.text: We all just want her out of our heads. We can't get her out. She sits at the top of our thoughts, sometimes a casual obsession, more often, a horrible beautiful daydream.

Destroyer of men and women alike, we adore her in spite, because of, for being exactly who she is. She's our muse, a rotten thing of perfection and imperfection entwined. She has no conscience, no thought for anyone but herself.

To spit on her face, to kiss her lips. That's why we love her. That's why we'll do anything to be near her, to help her, to put her on a pedestal to raise her higher and higher, further and further from the depths we sink to because of her.
We reach out. Call out. Scream out.
Caroline.
TITLES: SISTER CARRIE, BASED ON THE NOVEL BY THEODORE DREISER
A Bus Station
CHARLIE DROUET stands, reading his newspaper. His name imprinted on the newspaper itself. He wears a simple t-shirt with jeans.
His hair uncombed, his face slightly stubbly.
CAROLINE walks up to the bus overhang. She has a bag by her side. Her clothes are disheveled.
She is attractive, but nothing special at this time and place, still, the spark is there.
Charlie folds up his newspaper and walks over, looking her over just a bit.
Where you headed?
My sister's, not too far from here.
Where you from?
Small town, about three hours east. You'd have never heard of it.
Can I offer you a cigarette?
No thanks, don't smoke.
I insist you start or start back up.
Carrie takes the cigarette and he lights.
Thanks.
The Bus
They both sit on the bus. He is sitting next to her. They both steal looks at each other.
Each speaks to the camera in turn.
The window throws the city across both their faces, a frame at a time.
I'd like to think I charmed her, I'd like to think there was some instantaneous attraction neither of us could help or control.
When they think about me like this, I always look better, sound smarter than I really am. I'm really nothing special. I always insist, but they never seem to hear.

I was fantasizing about all the things I'd like to do to her, nothing super dirty. I mean, I wanted to see her naked, wanted to touch her. But it was all just casual sensual, just getting to know you fantasizing.
Charlie was real sweet, mostly harmless. Not the kind of guy I usually go for, exactly the kind of guy I know I'll end up hurting.

I'm taking creative license with this whole introduction scene, because I can't exactly be honest about how raw and honest our initial encounter felt. This is all in retrospect, all suspect to my emotion. Nothing objective.
I hope to strip it all away and make ourselves naked and somehow figure out just who this girl is.
Charlie's a passionate guy, but a bit naïve. Wears his heart on his sleeve. That can be really attractive in a guy.
Or not.
Charlie looks at Carrie. She looks back at him. He hands her his business card.
Look, I know you're new here. But if you need someone to show you around, help you get comfortable with the city, all you gotta do is let me know. I keep my own hours, so it's never a bother.
Thanks Charlie.
